transcript:
>> Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
The Protect College Sports Act has crossed the finish line in the Senate.
Senators passed a bill late Monday night by a 77 to 22 vote.
Texas Republican Senator Ted Cruz was a top negotiator.
>> This bill puts an end to the chaos plaguing college athletics.
It protects NIL opportunities because student athletes deserve the opportunity to benefit
from their talent without being taken advantage of by unscrupulous agents and backdoor deals.
>> The bill establishes a federal framework for college athletics to create one set system
on how athletes can earn money on their name, image and likeness.
It also caps the amount of money schools can share with their athletes and limits transfers
between schools.
Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito will not participate in an important climate change
case set for argument next week.
>> In Paris, Kerry Johnson reports a court clerk provided no explanation.
>> Environmental organizations and watchdog groups had been pressing Justice Alito'd
recuse himself from the case, in which Boulder, Colorado, suing the energy companies Suncor
and Exxon over local harms due to climate change.
Alito does not own stock in those energy giants, but his financial disclosure says he has investments
in Phillips 66 and ConocoPhillips.
>> Our watchdog says the decision to step aside is the right move.
Federal judges are required to step aside in cases where their impartiality might reasonably
be questioned, but at the Supreme Court, that decision is up to individual justices.
Kerry Johnson, NPR News.
>> The National Hurricane Center in Miami says life-threatening winds and flash flooding
are ongoing along the southern half of Mexico's Baja California Peninsula.
Hurricane Polo has made landfall, and the forecasters say they expect the storm to remain
a hurricane when it makes a second landfall over the Mexican mainland.
An airstrike by Myanmar's military and resistance-held territory has killed at least 35 people and
injured dozens more, and Michael Sullivan reports from neighboring Thailand.
>> The attack occurred around noon in Chow Dao in the west of the country, according
to the Arakan Army, the ethnic armed group that controls the area.
It said a military fighter jet dropped two bombs near a busy market, killing vendors,
shoppers, and other civilians.
A rescue official confirmed that account to the Associated Press and said the market was
one of the region's main wholesale centers, drawing vendors and customers from all over
the state.
The military has stepped up airstrikes against resistance groups in the last year.
More than 100,000 people have died with millions more displaced in the civil war that's followed
the military's 2021 coup.
For NPR News, I'm Michael Sullivan in Chiang Rai.
>> And you're listening to NPR News.
The U.S. Navy says two Navy aviators are being evaluated by medical personnel after they
were forced to eject from their aircraft.
The Navy says the incident happened off the coast of Virginia during aircraft recovery
operations aboard the USS Dwight D. Eisenhower, and that four Navy personnel on board were
injured.
British police say that five men arrested near a U.S.-run base in England will be released
on bail.
The U.K.'s head of counterterrorism policing says the men face stringent conditions and
remain under investigation.
Investigators are looking into a possible link to Iran, Russia, or non-state-backed
military groups.
A towering figure of Caribbean music who performed as Mighty Sparrow has died in New York at age
91.
NPR's Felix Contreras reports on Slinger Francisco.
>> Slinger Francisco earned his stage name Mighty Sparrow for his energetic dance moves
during his earliest performances in the dual island nation of Trinidad and Tobago.
And it was during the island's legendary Calypso Carnival competitions when his legend began
to take shape by way of lyrics that were socially conscious about everyday life on the islands.
Mighty Sparrow was considered the Calypso King of the World by his fans and recognized
by the island's cultural institutions for spreading the sound of the West African-based
Calypso from the Caribbean to the world.
Felix Contreras, NPR News.

topics.text: Senate passes Protect College Sports Act 77-22, establishing federal NIL framework for student athletes
Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito recuses himself from climate change case involving Boulder v. energy companies
Hurricane Polo makes landfall on Mexico's Baja California Peninsula with life-threatening winds and flooding
Myanmar military airstrike kills at least 35 people near market in Arakan Army-controlled territory
Two Navy aviators eject from aircraft during operations aboard USS Dwight D. Eisenhower off Virginia
Five men arrested near U.S. base in England released on bail pending investigation
Mighty Sparrow, legendary Caribbean calypso musician Slinger Francisco, dies in New York at 91
